blocks.raw: <WikiCalloutBox title="Rolling Sphere Radii (IEC 62305-3)" variant="info">Each protection level has a defined radius: **Level I = 20 m**, **Level II = 30 m**, **Level III = 45 m**, **Level IV = 60 m**. These radii determine the maximum distance from air terminals at which protection extends. In the Philippines, Level II and III systems are most common for commercial and residential buildings.</WikiCalloutBox>

blocks.raw:
<Example title="Ground Resistance Calculation">
**Scenario:** Metro Manila building with clay soil (resistivity 120 ohms·m), requires ≤10 ohms.

**Rod specification:** Two 3.5 m deep copper rods, 16 mm diameter, spaced 5.5 m apart (1.5× length rule).

**Calculation:**
- Single rod: R = ρ / L = 120 / 3.5 ≈ 34 ohms
- Two rods in parallel (approximate): R_parallel ≈ 34 / 2 = 17 ohms (overestimate; actual lower due to spacing reduction factor)
- With spacing factor k ≈ 0.6: R ≈ 17 × 0.6 ≈ 10.2 ohms (marginal)

**Improvement:** Add horizontal strap or ring conductor buried 1 m deep around rod cluster.
- Ring adds ~5 ohms capacitance (parallel path)
- Final system: R ≈ (10.2 × 5) / (10.2 + 5) ≈ 3.4 ohms (well below 10 ohm target)

**Test:** Verify with clamp-on tester at three points on system perimeter; all ≤10 ohms confirms compliance.
</Example>

blocks.raw: <WikiCalloutBox title="PD 1096 Requirements for Tall Buildings (UK Standard, Reference)" variant="warning">PD 1096 does not specify LPS; PEC references NFPA 780 (45m RSM radius) for all structures. For tall residential towers and commercial buildings exceeding 50 m in Philippine cities, use RSM with Level II protection minimum. Mesh conductor spacing ≤10 m required on roofs of structures >50 m to ensure comprehensive coverage and current distribution redundancy.</WikiCalloutBox>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={[{"mistake": "Using only one down conductor on a building. Single point of failure means entire structure unprotected if that conductor fails during strike.","correction": "Install minimum two independent down conductors per PEC Article 2.50. Preferred: one per corner of rectangular buildings. Ensures redundancy and current distribution."},{"mistake": "Accepting ground resistance >15 ohms. Marginal resistance increases voltage rise during strike, risking step and touch hazards.","correction": "Design grounding system to achieve ≤10 ohms. Use parallel rods, deep electrodes, or ring conductors combined. Test with clamp-on tester after installation."},{"mistake": "Running down conductors through occupied spaces (inside walls, along window edges). Strikes produce 30 kA+ currents; voltage rise creates electrocution risk.","correction": "Route down conductors on exterior surfaces only. Maintain ≥1.8 m clearance from windows, doors, balconies per NFPA 780. Use insulated supports or conduit for added safety."},{"mistake": "Bonding metal roof equipment with undersized wire (e.g., 6 mm² copper instead of 16 mm² minimum).","correction": "All bonding must use ≥16 mm² copper or ≥25 mm² aluminum per PEC. Undersized bonding can fuse during strike, creating hazard."},{"mistake": "Installing air terminals with ball-end design on residential buildings. Belief that ball is more effective.","correction": "Ball and sharp terminals are equivleant per IEC 62305. Choose based on aesthetics or regional preference. Ensure terminal ≥0.5 m above roof, properly secured."},{"mistake": "Neglecting bonding of solar panel frames. Assumption that PV systems are isolated.","correction": "Solar panels are metal structures exposed to direct lightning. Bond frames to down conductor system within 2 m. Bond DC strings and inverter chassis via SPD to grounding network."}]} />

blocks.raw: <Callout type="info" title="Design Documentation Package">For any structure requiring LPS in the Philippines, prepare:**• Building layout with LPS component locations (plan and elevation views)• Air terminal specifications and placement rationlea (RSM verification)• Down conductor routing and bonding schedule• Grounding electrode design and soil resistivity test results• Calculated zone of protection diagram• Maintenance schedule and testing intervals• Compliance statement referencing PEC Part 2 and IEC 62305**This package becomes the basis for LEA licensing exam questions and site inspection.** </Callout>
